secondSource.note: CIQUAL's skinless cooked breast is pan-fried rather than grilled; both are cooked without skin.
Same food, different national measurements: USDA's egg carries 10.6 g fat/100 g against CIQUAL's 8.6 g, a 15.7% energy gap.

fr.name: œufs
fr.note: AGROVOC types "oeuf"; French writes the ligature, and the plural adds the s.

secondSource.note: Same food, different cooked moisture: CIQUAL's cooked rice is drier, 11.5% more energy per 100 g.
Dry oats, the weight the templates buy; the cooking step adds water, not energy.
CIQUAL 2020 has no cooked buckwheat entry; its raw value is recorded for traceability only and is not comparable.
CIQUAL's plain fresh cream cheese at 3% fat stands in for US cottage cheese at 2%.

nl.name: hüttenkäse
nl.note: Dutch shops sell both this and the loan "cottage cheese"; this is the Danone and Albert Heijn wording.

fr.name: cottage cheese
fr.note: French and Belgian shops print the English loan; "fromage blanc" is a different product.

bg.name: извара
bg.note: Closest locally sold product; cottage cheese is not sold in mainstream Bulgarian retail.

secondSource.note: CIQUAL's plain-yogurt average spans fat levels; USDA's item is whole milk.
CIQUAL's generic apple has no energy value; the Golden variety is the cross-check.
CIQUAL has no mixed-nuts entry; grilled cashew is the closest nut item.

nl.name: tomaten
nl.note: Wikidata's label names the plant; the shop word is the fruit's plural alias.

bg.name: леща
bg.note: Wikidata holds no Bulgarian label for the lentil.

secondSource.note: CIQUAL's boiled chickpeas hold more water than USDA's row (17.7 g carbohydrate against 27.4 g), so its energy is 10.4% lower; both are boiled, drained chickpeas.

de.name: Kabeljau
de.note: Wikidata's label names the species (Atlantischer Kabeljau); German shelves print the food's own word, and AGROVOC's German term carries no published licence.

bg.name: пълнозърнест хляб
bg.note: Wikidata holds no Bulgarian label for wholemeal bread.

nl.name: tofu
nl.note: Albert Heijn, Jumbo and Delhaize all print the loan word "tofu"; Wikidata's Dutch label is the alternative spelling "tofoe".
